newsitem.title: USA: Internet goes high-yld - Verio plans $150 mln deal.
newsitem.headline: Internet goes high-yld - Verio plans $150 mln deal.

text.p: National business-oriented internet service provider (ISP) Verio Inc on Friday said proceeds from an upcoming $150 million high-yield debt offering will pave the way for acquisitions of as many as 31 regional ISPs within one year.
That would more than double Verio's current network of wholly- or majority-owned regional providers, which currently stands at 19, said Verio spokesman Steven Silvers.

"The money from the debt offering would give us a bigger war chest to continue acquisitions and the operations and building of the network," Silvers said. "The timing is right -- we've raised $100 million in private investments over the past year and so far we have carried no debt," he said.
"So the company feels confident it's a good time to get some leverage," he added.

Investors in Verio include Norwest Venture Capital, Brooks Fiber Properties Inc, The Centennial Funds, Telecom Partners, Fleet Equity Partners, Bessemer Venture Partners, Boston Capital Ventures and Providence Equity Partners, according to the company's home page on the internet.
The deal, managed via underwriters Merrill Lynch & Co Inc and Lazard Freres & Co, would be the first offering from a pure-play internet company, according to market sources.

Underwriters and Verio's Silvers declined to comment on details of the offering. Other sources said the deal would be priced as seven-year senior notes with a two-and-a-half year prefunded interest reserve.
Pricing is expected next week, sources added.

Verio was founded in 1996 as World-Net Access Inc by veterans of the internet and telecommunications industries. The company is building a national network that combines the strength of a high-speed backbone with the service of local and regional internet providers, it said.

Regional affiliates of Verio include Global Enterprise Services Inc (GES) of Princeton, N.J., NorthWestNet Inc of Belleview, Wash., OnRamp Technologies of Dallas, Texas; and Network Intensive of Irvine, Calif.
Verio, based in Denver, Colo., plans to have a presence in all major U.S. markets in the next six to 12 months.
